You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE course (
    Course_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Staring_Date TEXT,
    Course TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Course_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE teacher (
    Teacher_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age TEXT,
    Hometown TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Teacher_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE course_arrange (
    Course_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Teacher_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Grade INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (Course_ID, Teacher_ID, Grade),
    UNIQUE (Course_ID, Teacher_ID, Grade),
    FOREIGN KEY (Teacher_ID) REFERENCES teacher(Teacher_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Course_ID) REFERENCES course(Course_ID)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

To view the course schedule datasheet with course, starting date, teacher, and grade:

```sql
SELECT
    c.Course_ID,
    c.Course,
    c.Staring_Date,
    t.Teacher_ID,
    t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
    ca.Grade
FROM course AS c
JOIN course_arrange AS ca
    ON c.Course_ID = ca.Course_ID
JOIN teacher AS t
    ON ca.Teacher_ID = t.Teacher_ID
ORDER BY c.Staring_Date, c.Course_ID, ca.Grade;
```
I need the list to show which courses each teacher teaches.

```sql
SELECT
    t.Teacher_ID,
    t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
    c.Course_ID,
    c.Course,
    c.Staring_Date,
    ca.Grade
FROM teacher AS t
JOIN course_arrange AS ca
    ON t.Teacher_ID = ca.Teacher_ID
JOIN course AS c
    ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
ORDER BY t.Name, c.Course, ca.Grade;
```
make sure the list only shows the teacher name and the course

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
    c.Course
FROM teacher AS t
JOIN course_arrange AS ca
    ON t.Teacher_ID = ca.Teacher_ID
JOIN course AS c
    ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
ORDER BY t.Name, c.Course;
```
the list should also be sorted alphabetically by the teachers' names

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
    c.Course
FROM teacher AS t
JOIN course_arrange AS ca
    ON t.Teacher_ID = ca.Teacher_ID
JOIN course AS c
    ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
ORDER BY t.Name ASC, c.Course ASC;
```
